semantics.identity_rule: Each concrete module instance has a stable instance identity.
semantics.definition_rule: Instance references exact Universal Module definition/version.
semantics.data_rule: Local data is scoped to the full instance identity, not merely module type.
semantics.isolation_rule: Different instances do not share mutable state unless explicit relation/shared-resource semantics say so.
semantics.lifecycle_rule: Definition, configured instance, enabled instance and running state remain separate.
semantics.authority_rule: Instance visibility does not grant read/write/lifecycle authority.

invariants.rule: Composition never silently transfers semantic ownership: universal modules own their primitives, domains own their composition semantics, and composed members retain their own identities and contracts.

Containment, relation, dependency, composition and projection edges exist only through explicit typed references; naming, file hierarchy, UI adjacency or shared values never create semantic structure.

hard_gates.condition: module type used as instance identity
